nodes.summary: The projector $P = |000\rangle\langle 000| + |111\rangle\langle 111|$ of the bit-flip code is self-adjoint and idempotent: $P^{*} = P$ and $P^2 = P$. These are the hypotheses on $P$ in the Knill–Laflamme theorem. The proof is entrywise: $P$ is diagonal with entries $0$ and $1$.
nodes.title: The code projector is an orthogonal projector

nodes.summary: Index the basis states of three qubits by $v \in \mathbb{F}_2^3$. The code space of the bit-flip code is spanned by $|000\rangle$ and $|111\rangle$, and its orthogonal projector is the diagonal matrix The encoding is $a|0\rangle + b|1\rangle \mapsto a|000\rangle + b|111\rangle$; each three-qubit cluster of Shor's nine-qubit code (Preskill, equation (7.1)) uses the same pair of states in the rotated basis…
nodes.title: Code space of the three-qubit bit-flip code

nodes.summary: On the code spanned by $|000\rangle$ and $|111\rangle$, the four errors $I, X_1, X_2, X_3$ (no error, or a bit flip on one of the three qubits) are correctable by one recovery channel. This is Preskill's remark in Section 7.1 that "a three-qubit code would suffice to protect against a single bit flip".
nodes.title: The three-qubit bit-flip code corrects any single bit flip

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be the projector onto the span of $|000\rangle$ and $|111\rangle$, and let $E$ and $E'$ be the identity or a single bit flip. Then These are the Knill–Laflamme conditions in Preskill's form (7.19), with $C$ the identity matrix: the code is nondegenerate for this error set (equation (7.15)).
nodes.title: Knill–Laflamme conditions for the bit-flip code

nodes.summary: The Pauli operator $Z_1 Z_4 Z_7 = X^0 Z^b$, with $b = e_0 + e_3 + e_6$ supported on the first qubit of each block, has weight three, and there is no scalar $\lambda$ with for the two Shor codewords. So the distance condition of Preskill's equation (7.34) fails at weight three, and the distance of Shor's code is at most three.
nodes.title: Shor's code has distance at most three

nodes.title: Shor's code has distance three

nodes.summary: Shor's code encodes one qubit into nine. Its basis codewords repeat a three-qubit cat state three times (Preskill, equation (7.1)): In Lean they are defined without the factor $2^{-3/2}$, as functions on the basis $\mathbb{F}_2^9$: for $x \in \mathbb{F}_2$, the amplitude of $|v\rangle$ in $|\bar x\rangle$ is $0$ unless each block $v_0 v_1 v_2$, $v_3 v_4 v_5$, $v_6 v_7 v_8$ is $000$ or $111$, and is then…
nodes.title: Codewords of Shor's nine-qubit code

nodes.summary: The errors corrected by the bit-flip code are indexed by `Option (Fin 3)`: `none` stands for no error, with flip pattern $0 \in \mathbb{F}_2^3$, and `some i` for a bit flip on qubit $i$, with flip pattern the unit vector $e_i$. The corresponding operator is the Pauli operator $X^{e} = X^{e} Z^{0}$ of CSS codes, so the error set is $\{I, X_1, X_2, X_3\}$.
